subject: StoneRiver integration: auth & SDK plan — post-demo action items

Subject: StoneRiver integration: auth & SDK plan — post-demo action items

Hi Amira / Rajiv — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align on an integration path that meets your security and data-flow needs.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: embeddings + light reranking for search relevance; occasional tool-calling for data enrichment.
- Preference for server-to-server model (no end-user browser tokens).
- Compliance: audit logs and short-lived credentials are must-haves; rotation policy required.

Recommendations (high-level)
1) Auth model: Service accounts with short-lived JWTs (15m TTL) minted by your identity provider via OIDC or by Redwood-managed token service — avoids long-lived API keys.
2) Key rotation: automate via KMS/HSM-backed keys and rotate signing keys quarterly; immediate revocation path for compromise.
3) SDK onboarding: we'll provide a lightweight SDK quickstart (Go/Node/Python) that supports automatic token refresh and structured-output tooling.
4) Routing & fallbacks: route high-priority production traffic to Dedicated pool; dev/test can use hosted endpoints.

Action items / owners
- Marcus (me): share a short technical plan + attachments (audit scope + schema) — attached.
- Soojin: put together a 1-page auth runbook + sample token flow and sample code.
- Ben: confirm cost estimate for dedicated capacity for the expected QPS.
- Amira/Rajiv: confirm whether you need support for in-house KMS or if Redwood-managed keys are acceptable.

Proposed next meeting: Fri Nov 20, 09:00 PT — 30m sync (tech + security). If that works, I’ll send an invite.

Attachments: stoneriver-ma-audit-scope.pdf, stoneriver-mvp-schema.xlsx

Thanks —

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful, appreciate the clear next steps. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side:

- Rotation window: 15m TTL for JWTs sounds fine for live requests. Does Redwood support automatic refresh using a short-lived signing key so we never ship long-lived private keys?
- Audit logs: can you scope exactly what’s captured (request id, model id, input hash, response id, token subject)? We need to map that to our internal audit schema.
- Compromise response: if a service account is suspected compromised, what is the fastest revocation path? We need <1 hour full revocation and a way to revoke by client id.

Also, slightly related — we use HashiCorp Vault for secrets. Would prefer Redwood to integrate with our Vault (so keys live in Vault) rather than handing over private keys, if possible.

Rajiv is on copy — he’ll chime in on the Vault integration and the compliance timeline.

Thanks,

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:42:20 -0800
Subject: RE: StoneRiver integration: auth & SDK plan — post-demo action items

Marcus / Ben — putting together the technical proposal in-line below; I’ll attach a quickstart bundle separately (redwood-sdk-quickstart.tar.gz).

Proposal (detailed)
- Token model: issue short-lived signing tokens (JWT) signed with a rotating RSA keypair stored in either Redwood KMS or a customer KMS (Vault/HSM) — we support both.
  - Token TTL: default 15 minutes; refresh endpoint returns new token signed by latest key.
  - Audience/scopes: tokens include aud="redwood:inference" and scope="embeddings:write,models:invoke" to allow per-route checks.
- Rotation & revocation:
  - Key rotation: automated 90-day rotation for signing keys; immediate roll-over supported.
  - Compromise: we publish a revocation list endpoint and support client-id revocation; revocation becomes effective within 60s for new tokens and we can revoke active refresh sessions within <1 hour via session blacklist.
- Integration patterns:
  1) Preferred (recommended): Customer-managed KMS + OIDC identity provider -> Redwood mints tokens on exchange. No private keys are exported.
  2) Alternate: Redwood-managed signing keys + customer stores private material in Redwood KMS (common for smaller customers).
- SDK behavior:
  - SDK automatically rotates tokens, retries idempotently on 401, and exposes a TokenProvider interface so you can plug in Vault-backed token fetch.
  - Example (pseudo-code snippet):

  // fetch short-lived token
  provider = new VaultTokenProvider({aud: 'redwood:inference', ttl: 900})
  token = provider.getToken()
  client = new RedwoodClient({token: token})
  client.embed(['query text'])

- Audit logging:
  - We capture request id, model version, client_id, time, and a cryptographic input hash (one-way) to satisfy PII minimization. Logs are exportable to your GCS/S3 or SIEM via streaming.

Open items for StoneRiver
- Confirm Vault integration preference (API-only or Vault Agent).
- Confirm whether you want rolling 90-day key rotation or stricter 30/60-day policy.
- Agree on production cutover window (Ben to estimate Dedicated capacity cost).

I’ll attach the SDK quickstart and a sample auth-runbook.

Soojin Lee

soojin.lee@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: StoneRiver integration: auth & SDK plan — post-demo action items

Amira / Rajiv — thanks for the questions and for highlighting Vault. Quick answers and next steps below.

- Vault integration: we support Vault Agent and API-based integrations. Recommended pattern is customer-managed KMS + OIDC exchange (no key material leaves your Vault). So yes, Vault-first is supported.
- Audit logs scope: request_id, model_id/version, client_id, timestamp, input_hash (SHA-256), response_id. We’ll map these fields to your schema; see attached stoneriver-mvp-schema.xlsx.
- Revocation SLA: Redwood can support emergency revocation — policy and tooling ensure client-id revocation is effective within 1 hour and token blacklist prevents new tokens immediately.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Technical sync (Soojin + Rajiv) to walk the Vault+OIDC flow (30m) — Tue Nov 24, 10:00 PT.
2) Ben to send a Dedicated capacity estimate (EOB Nov 20).
3) Marcus to circulate a draft SOW/contract; please review and we’ll incorporate contract-level SLAs.

Links: HubSpot:HS-124589 | Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBExampleSR | DocuSign:Envelope-ABC123

I’ll drop a calendar invite for the technical sync once you confirm Tue 24th works.
